destination.title: Supergravity, string constructions and quantum consistency
destination.question: How do supergravity descriptions, string constructions and quantum-consistency tests constrain one another across their distinct regimes?
destination.summary: The original proposal supplies candidate memberships without an independently justified scientific scope. A broad family is usable if it distinguishes deriving effective theories, testing their completion, classifying global data and studying particular limits. Shared terminology or source-parent relations do not establish equivalent questions.

systems: Supergravity theories with source-specific dimensions and supersymmetry
String/M/F-theory constructions and their effective descriptions
Related nongravitational theories and mathematical constructions as alternate or comparison homes
targets: Necessary consistency constraints and comparison with known constructions
Global moduli, discrete data and duality
Effective actions, vacua, amplitudes and defects
regimes: Perturbative and nonperturbative regimes remain distinct
Massless supergravity, massive multiplets and nongravitational limits remain distinct
Finite-distance constructions and infinite-distance limits remain distinct
assumptions: Conjectures and conditional construction proposals are retained as questions
No universal string realization or quantum-completeness theorem is assumed
conventions: Numerical membership and selectionRole are retrieval provenance
Ordinary and pre-Swampland work remains eligible
Source dates and exact original questions remain attached to their source records
includes: A broad family with several independently scoped questions
Useful methodological, application and alternate-home connections
excludes: Treating all members as one canonical question
Promoting source-local claims or graph relations into shared physical premises
Inferring current scientific status from archived descriptions

sources.title: Reggeization of N=8 supergravity and N=4 Yang-Mills theory. II.

evidence.text: Could singularities generated by perturbative gravitational graph sums encode the nonperturbative light states expected in a string-theory decoupling limit? The proposed connection is intended to bear on whether N=8 supergravity can stand as a complete quantum gravity.

sources.title: Stringy KLT relations, global symmetries, and $E_{7(7)}$ violation

evidence.text: How do stringy KLT relations organize SU(8)-violating massless amplitudes, and, after isolating the SU(8)-invariant R4 completion, do its single-soft scalar limits satisfy the continuous E7(7) requirement for an N=8 supergravity counterterm?

sources.title: Laplacian spectrum on a nilmanifold, truncations and effective theories

evidence.text: Does a finite reduction capture low-energy states, lift every solution, or satisfy a supergravity construction? The source treats these as distinct questions; differential closure alone is not a physical low-energy proof.

sources.title: Supersymmetric Protection and the Swampland

evidence.text: Can a four-dimensional quantum-gravity theory have an exactly vanishing N = 1 superpotential, or no N = 2 prepotential instanton corrections, when its realized supersymmetry permits those contributions?

sources.title: Compactness of brane moduli and the String Lamppost Principle in d > 6

evidence.text: Can compactness, connectedness, and local field-theory data of small-instanton brane moduli reconstruct internal string geometries and establish the String Lamppost Principle for supersymmetric gravity in dimensions seven through nine, with an extension toward six dimensions?

sources.title: New supersymmetric string theories from discrete theta angles

evidence.text: When do discrete theta angles define physically distinct quantum gravities with identical massless supergravity, and how do they change massive spectra, dualities and BPS completeness in compactifications with sixteen supercharges?

sources.title: New supersymmetric string moduli spaces from frozen singularities

evidence.text: Can inequivalent configurations with the same frozen ADE singularity type define disconnected moduli spaces of theories with sixteen supercharges, distinguished by lattice data and global gauge topology? Can their decompactification patterns predict an additional nine-dimensional rank-one theory?

sources.title: Quantum gravity bounds on $ \mathcal{N} $ = 1 effective theories in four dimensions

evidence.text: Which axionic couplings and gauge sectors can be compatible with quantum gravity in four-dimensional N=1 supergravity?

sources.title: The geometry of hypermultiplets

evidence.text: Review the geometry of hypermultiplets coupled to supergravity, its realization in string compactifications, and whether negative-curvature quaternion-Kähler geometry suffices for a string realization or admits swampland examples.

sources.title: Bounds on discrete gauge symmetries in supergravity

evidence.text: What upper bounds constrain finite cyclic gauge symmetries acting on massless moduli at enhanced-symmetry loci in supergravity with at least eight supercharges, and which bounds are attained by string constructions?

sources.title: The landscape and the swampland of O(3,3) gauged supergravities

evidence.text: Which seven-dimensional half-maximal O(3,3) gaugings admit exact type II freely acting orbifold realizations, and how do string consistency conditions restrict their continuous gauging parameters?

sources.title: Quantum Gravity Principles for 4d $\mathcal{N}=2$ Supergravity Theories and Asymptotic Hodge Theory

evidence.text: Which asymptotic properties of 4d N=2 vector multiplet moduli spaces follow from supersymmetry alone, and which require quantum gravity input concerning light towers, charge completeness and compatible gravitational duality frames?

sources.title: Gauged D=9 supergravities and Scherk-Schwarz reduction

evidence.text: Which inequivalent nine-dimensional gauged theories arise from twisted circle reductions of IIB supergravity and string theory, and how do monodromy conjugacy classes determine their gaugings and allowed parameters?

sources.title: Distinguishing off-shell supergravities with on-shell physics

evidence.text: Can off-shell completions of four-dimensional N=1 supergravity that agree locally on shell be distinguished by global supersymmetric compactifications or physical boundary degrees of freedom?

sources.title: The String landscape and the swampland

evidence.text: Can a fully consistent four-dimensional N=2 theory have a low-energy spectrum consisting only of the scalar-free supergravity multiplet? Known string examples instead contain additional scalars associated with quantities such as coupling or internal volume.

sources.title: Consistent gravitino couplings in nonsupersymmetric strings

evidence.text: How can the massless ten-dimensional gravitino interact consistently with nonsupersymmetric open-string matter in the USp(32) Type I string, and what leading low-energy action realizes the required consistency?

sources.title: Reggeization of N=8 supergravity and N=4 Yang-Mills theory. II.

evidence.text: Identify a common leading-logarithm kernel and factorial ladder combinatorics, sum the exponential, then restore separate Born contributions and symmetry projections. The application dictionary distinguishes the gauge prefactor from the gravitational loop prefactor.

sources.title: Stringy KLT relations, global symmetries, and $E_{7(7)}$ violation

evidence.text: Closed-string amplitudes are obtained through KLT from α′-expanded ordered open-string amplitudes. Supersymmetry Ward identities supply missing six-point NMHV components from a five-amplitude basis; the authors automate this construction in Mathematica using supplied open-string amplitude code.

sources.title: Laplacian spectrum on a nilmanifold, truncations and effective theories

evidence.text: Linearize around a higher-dimensional solution, expand in internal eigenmodes, and analyze kinetic and mass mixing before selecting light states. The kinetic terms also determine the proper distances needed for a distance-conjecture test.

sources.title: Supersymmetric Protection and the Swampland

evidence.text: Test the candidate wrapping cycle for the stated H-flux anomaly and remove the forbidden configuration. This is a cycle-specific selection rule associated with a gauged isometry, rather than a zero-mode-lifting calculation.

sources.title: Compactness of brane moduli and the String Lamppost Principle in d > 6

evidence.text: In 9d, use the piecewise cubic 5d prepotential: its second derivative determines the inverse gauge coupling and its third derivative the Chern-Simons coefficient. Single-valuedness around the interval's double cover requires the total level jump ∑i ci=0.

sources.title: New supersymmetric string theories from discrete theta angles

evidence.text: Compare theta-dependent instanton phases with anomalous disconnected O(32) transformations; use D-brane Chern–Simons couplings and induced string charge to distinguish removable parameters from physical ones.

sources.title: Bootstrapping string theory EFT

evidence.text: How tightly do four-point monodromy relations and unitarity constrain open-string EFT coefficients, spacetime dimension and spectra, with or without supersymmetry and tachyons? What closed-string regions follow through KLT?

sources.title: Hyperbolic spaces in string and M theory

evidence.text: Which string and eleven-dimensional supergravity backgrounds can contain negatively curved symmetric spaces or finite-volume hyperbolic quotients, and what do these constructions imply for supersymmetry, dimensional reduction, gravitational potentials and candidate holographic conformal theories?

sources.title: Wormholes in Maximal Supergravity

evidence.text: Can covering-space supergravity saddles be interpreted in a string theory whose scalar space is an arithmetic quotient? The paper uses exact discrete gauge symmetry, rather than the broken continuous classical isometry, as the constraint on such an interpretation.

sources.title: Gopakumar-Vafa invariants and the Emergent String Conjecture

evidence.text: Do gauge-coupling asymptotics and charged BPS indices distinguish decompactification from emergent-string limits in five-dimensional supergravity, and do Calabi-Yau data satisfy the resulting geometric predictions of the Emergent String Conjecture?

sources.title: Seeking the Loop Quantum Gravity Barbero-Immirzi Parameter and Field in 4D, N = 1 Supergravity

evidence.text: Can the constant and dynamical Barbero–Immirzi coupling be embedded in four-dimensional N=1 supergravity, and does its supersymmetric completion support an axion interpretation suggesting overlap with string effective theory?

sources.title: One loop superstring effective actions and N=8 supergravity

evidence.text: Can pure four-dimensional N=8 supergravity be separated from states and interactions required by its proposed string origin?

sources.title: D term strings

evidence.text: Which local magnetic cosmic strings preserve supersymmetry in four-dimensional N=1 supergravity, how does their gravitational BPS bound work, and could these solitons describe effective D-strings from wrapped D-branes?

sources.title: String dualities and modular symmetries in supergravity: a review

evidence.text: How do modular symmetries supplement four-dimensional N=1 and N=2 supergravity to constrain effective couplings, expose nonperturbative dualities, and encode quantum-gravity information such as the moduli-dependent species scale?

sources.title: A unique coupling of the massive spin-2 field to supergravity

evidence.text: Which leading gravitational couplings of a massive spin-2 supermultiplet are compatible with undeformed four-dimensional N=1 supergravity, and what do they imply for an isolated massive spin-2 effective theory?

sources.title: TASI Lectures on Supergravity and String Vacua in Various Dimensions

evidence.text: How strongly does quantum consistency constrain low-energy supersymmetric theories coupled to gravity, and how closely do those constraints match known string constructions in dimensions 10, 8, and 6?

sources.title: Generalizations of the double-copy: the KLT bootstrap

evidence.text: Which generalized tree-level KLT kernels define local double-copy maps, which single-copy theories satisfy their constraints, and which output theories can they produce?

sources.title: Fine Tuning, Sequestering, and the Swampland

evidence.text: Can multiple conformal points remain independently tunable in one compact gravitational theory? The orbifold construction supplies 27 local sectors and Coulomb parameters that can all be set to zero independently.

sources.title: Swampland Constraints on 5d $\mathcal{N}=1$ Supergravity

evidence.text: Which five-dimensional theories with eight supercharges can consistently couple to gravity? The paper tests bulk matter and Chern–Simons data through the quantum consistency of magnetic strings and compares those tests with restrictions from compact Calabi–Yau geometry.

sources.title: String universality

evidence.text: Can the five perturbative string theories and 11D supergravity share a central domain with identical 4D low energy physics, and can duality-related boundary descriptions constrain moduli stabilization, supersymmetry breaking, and phenomenology there?

sources.title: Symmetry points of $ \mathcal{N}=1 $ modular geometry

evidence.text: How far can modular symmetry alone identify critical points and generically classify their vacuum energy in four-dimensional N=1 supergravity, while constraining weak-coupling potential asymptotics through metric positivity and imposed Swampland criteria?

sources.title: Arguments Against a Finite N=8 Supergravity

evidence.text: Can an all-orders finite, SU(8)-covariant perturbative S-matrix for N = 8 supergravity describe a quantum-gravitational theory containing charged BPS states, given their proposed production amplitudes and dispersion-theoretic contributions at low energy?

sources.title: Reggeization of N=8 supergravity and N=4 Yang-Mills theory. II.

evidence.text: Can perturbatively finite four-dimensional N=8 supergravity admit a nonperturbative completion and reproduce the light-state phenomena associated with a string-theory decoupling limit? Regge trajectories and cuts are investigated as possible perturbative clues rather than a resolution.

sources.title: Supersymmetric Objects in Gauged Supergravities

evidence.text: How do supersymmetric gravitational objects admit tractable low-energy descriptions in supergravity, and how can lower-dimensional black objects and flows be related to microscopic branes and holographic field theories?

sources.title: Three-forms, dualities and membranes in four-dimensional supergravity

evidence.text: How can four-dimensional N=1 supergravity with double three-form multiplets accommodate symplectic dualities, membranes with arbitrary electric-magnetic charges, and back-reacted BPS domain walls connecting different flux vacua?

sources.title: A Note on Membrane Interactions and the Scalar potential

evidence.text: Can a membrane interaction dictionary convert restrictions on quantum-gravity spectra into restrictions on scalar potentials, and can the construction extend beyond four-dimensional N=1 supergravity?

sources.title: One loop superstring effective actions and N=8 supergravity

evidence.text: The paper tests compatibility between curvature interactions inherited from compactified strings and supersymmetry of the four-dimensional massless theory.

sources.title: Gravitino Swampland Conjecture

evidence.text: Can an alternative supergravity formulation remain regular at zero c_s² or zero coupled-field determinant, and can it arise as a low-energy limit of string theory?

sources.title: String theory from maximal supersymmetry

evidence.text: How strongly do maximal supersymmetry, unbroken R-symmetry, higher-point tree factorization, and a six-scalar parity condition constrain four-point EFT Wilson coefficients? With additional dispersive positivity assumptions, do those constraints isolate the open-superstring Veneziano amplitude?

sources.title: TASI Lectures on Remnants from the String Landscape

evidence.text: How can ten- or eleven-dimensional theories yield four-dimensional gauge and gravitational physics?

sources.title: All eight- and nine-dimensional string vacua from junctions

evidence.text: Can string and 5-brane junctions, extended to O7+ planes, describe all known 8d theories with 16 supercharges, determine their global gauge groups and recover the 9d string-vacuum branches through decompactification limits?

sources.title: Four-dimensional $\mathbf{\mathcal{N}=4}$ SYM theory and the swampland

evidence.text: Does quantum-gravity consistency impose an intrinsic bound on massless matter, independently of the range of known string compactifications? The paper examines Minkowski theories with 16 supercharges as a test of the conjectured completeness of the string landscape.

sources.title: Local SU(5) Unification from the Heterotic String

evidence.text: Can local FI sources and the full supergravity fields support an N = 1 background with two dimensions much larger than the string scale? Can an isotropic supersymmetric vacuum be obtained as a limit?

sources.title: Swampland Constraints on 5d $\mathcal{N}=1$ Supergravity

evidence.text: Which necessary constraints on matter content and cubic and mixed gauge/gravitational Chern–Simons couplings follow from unitary monopole-string worldsheets and Calabi–Yau divisor geometry in 5d N=1 supergravity?

sources.title: Supersymmetry breaking with fields, strings and branes

evidence.text: How do supersymmetry-breaking mechanisms connect four-dimensional field theory and supergravity to string constructions, and what can tadpole-deformed backgrounds establish about vacuum stability and the onset of inflation?

sources.title: Classification of ten-dimensional heterotic strings

evidence.text: Is the known list of ten-dimensional heterotic strings complete independently of free-field constructions, and how far can modular constraints classify meromorphic c=24 conformal field theories?

sources.title: Asymptotics of 5d supergravity theories and the emergent string conjecture

evidence.text: Can consistency of supergravity string probes classify infinite-distance limits of five-dimensional theories with eight supercharges, including uniqueness of the leading weakly coupled fields, and provide evidence for the Emergent String Conjecture without assuming a compactification origin?

sources.title: Triples, fluxes, and strings

evidence.text: Which discrete choices distinguish components of string moduli space with sixteen supersymmetries, primarily in seven or more dimensions, and which string/M/F theory descriptions realize the same component?

sources.title: One loop superstring effective actions and N=8 supergravity

evidence.text: Does the same-chirality Weyl quartic required by the reported compactified-string actions admit an N=8 completion within the massless supergravity multiplet, possibly with scalar couplings and corrected transformations?

sources.title: Anatomy of a top-down approach to discrete and modular flavor symmetry

evidence.text: How does a heterotic string construction determine the complete flavor symmetry and its breaking, and which restrictions might this impose on bottom-up discrete and modular flavor models?

sources.title: Nondecoupling of Maximal Supergravity from the Superstring

evidence.text: Can the maximal-supergravity multiplet be isolated from string theory while gravitational interactions remain at finite strength? The question requires examining additional nonperturbative states as well as perturbative string excitations.

sources.title: On extended supersymmetry of 4d Galileons and 3-brane effective actions

evidence.text: Can asymmetric brane boundaries reproduce the quintic amplitude patterns and their free parameters? Can massive-gravity limits explain the forced gravity couplings, and do N=2 hypermultiplets admit Galileons outside the vector-multiplet classification?

sources.title: The Moduli space and M(atrix) theory of 9d N=1 backgrounds of M/string theory

evidence.text: Determine the moduli-space components, weakly coupled limits and DLCQ M(atrix) descriptions of reduced-rank nine-dimensional M/string backgrounds preserving 16 supercharges.

sources.title: Populating the swampland: The Case of U(1)**496 and E(8) x U(1)**248

evidence.text: Do U(1)^496 and E8×U(1)^248 ten-dimensional supergravities possess quantum-gravity completions? The paper tests requirements on compactification moduli spaces and on the fate of supersymmetric naked singularities, without assuming a string construction.

sources.title: Three-forms and Fayet-Iliopoulos terms in Supergravity: Scanning Planck mass and BPS domain walls

evidence.text: Can a three-form embedded in a vector multiplet dynamically generate the supergravity Planck scale, admit a Fayet–Iliopoulos dual description, and support membrane domain walls across which the effective Planck mass changes?

sources.title: Saturating unitarity bounds at U-duality symmetric points

evidence.text: Where do the leading four-graviton Wilson coefficients of toroidally compactified type II string theory attain their minima in D=6,7,8, and can these values guide future tests of sharp unitarity bounds for maximally supersymmetric quantum gravity?

sources.title: $G_2$ flux compactifications

evidence.text: How can three-dimensional N=1 effective actions for the five ten-dimensional string theories be organized on general G2 geometries, including two-form sectors, axions, vectors, geometric flux and real superpotentials?

sources.title: String Universality in Six Dimensions

evidence.text: Do low-energy consistency conditions characterize the six-dimensional supersymmetric quantum-gravity theories, and does every such consistent theory admit a string compactification? The paper tests this through anomaly constraints, explicit K3 constructions and apparently exceptional infinite families.

sources.title: Supersymmetric Protection and the Swampland

evidence.text: Can a nonsupersymmetric quantum-gravity theory inherit exact vanishing or exact extremality saturation through a relation to a supersymmetric theory?

sources.title: Further refining the de Sitter swampland conjecture

evidence.text: Can explicit positive-potential supergravity points constrain conjectured quantum-gravity bounds? The paper uses classical type IIA data while tracking whether volume, coupling, flux quantization and source multiplicity permit a reliable string interpretation.

sources.title: Where is tree-level heterotic string theory?

evidence.text: Which string-like structures follow from four-point tree-level consistency in ten-dimensional half-maximal supersymmetry, and where do heterotic amplitudes lie relative to the resulting EFT bounds?

sources.title: Global Aspects of Moduli Spaces of 2d SCFTs

evidence.text: Can the Bagger–Witten bundle and its supporting moduli stack be defined intrinsically, constructed in further examples, and used to formulate a necessary criterion for UV completion of four-dimensional N=1 supergravity?

sources.title: Spin-four $ \mathcal{N}=7 $ W-supergravity: S-fold and double copy construction

evidence.text: Can a four-dimensional theory with 28 supercharges exist beyond conventional massless supergravity, using massive Weyl-multiplet double copies and nonperturbative string S-folds?

sources.title: Hyperbolic space forms and orbifold compactification in M-theory

evidence.text: Which string and supergravity backgrounds can contain real hyperbolic factors or finite-volume discrete quotients, and when do Killing spinors, finite flux and possible holographic interpretations survive the quotient construction?

destination.title: Scalar–curvature cosmology and neighboring inflation mechanisms
destination.question: How do scalar–curvature interactions alter cosmological evolution and perturbations, and how do their model-specific consistency tests compare with neighboring inflation mechanisms?
destination.summary: This is a proposed organizing scope. The original packet supplies numerical membership without a scientific region definition. Its Gauss–Bonnet core connects inflation, nonsingular cosmology and later evolution, while adjacent frameworks contribute comparisons and consistency questions.

systems: Scalar-dependent Gauss–Bonnet cosmologies with distinct gravitational sectors and field contents
Separate Chern–Simons, preferred-frame and nonminimal matter–curvature inflation models
Curvature EFTs for scalarization and gauge-matter theories with independent torsion
targets: Inflationary backgrounds, exits, reconstruction and perturbations
Primordial tensors, PBHs and scalar-induced gravitational waves
Reheating, late-time evolution and classical nonsingular solutions
Compatibility of additional gravitational phenomena with cosmic evolution
regimes: Slow roll, constant roll and two-field rapid turn where separately specified
Classical flat, open and closed FRW settings
Postinflationary and late-time regimes kept distinct from inflation
assumptions: No common luminal tensor condition, Swampland cut or Einstein–Hilbert approximation is inferred
Reported viability remains conditional on each source's model and dated benchmarks
conventions: Unit dispositions distinguish the Gauss–Bonnet core from boundary and alternate homes within this broader navigation family
Source settings, claims and graph relations are context rather than automatic question premises
A singleton preserves its exact source statement without asserting atomicity or cross-source uniqueness
includes: Distinct mechanisms and compound source questions with explicit qualifications
excludes: A claim that numerical proximity establishes scientific equivalence
Universal observational viability, renormalizability, stability or UV completion
A common single-field, slow-roll or luminal regime

sources.title: Higher Curvature Corrections to Primordial Fluctuations in Slow-roll Inflation

evidence.text: Can simultaneous Gauss–Bonnet and parity-violating curvature couplings modify primordial scalar/tensor spectra and gravitational-wave polarization during slow-roll inflation despite negligible energetic corrections?

sources.title: Inflation driven by Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity

evidence.text: Can a scalar-coupled Gauss–Bonnet term drive inflation and an exit while the Einstein term is retained, without assuming scalar slow roll? Does adding a scalar potential cure perturbative problems and allow subsequent Einstein-dominated evolution?

sources.title: Viable Inflation in Scalar-Gauss-Bonnet Gravity and Reconstruction from Observational Indices

evidence.text: Can scalar–Gauss–Bonnet coupling improve the inflationary phenomenology of cubic, quartic and exponential potentials, provide an exit mechanism, and permit reconstruction of a theory from prescribed H(N) and r(N)?

sources.title: Swampland implications of GW170817-compatible Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity

evidence.text: Can a Gauss–Bonnet interaction permit canonical inflation with an order-one potential slope and a limited field excursion while tensor propagation remains luminal and tensor production remains small?

sources.title: Pleasant behavior of swampland conjectures in the face of specific inflationary models

evidence.text: Can an inverse-potential Gauss–Bonnet coupling reconcile single-field slow-roll inflation with distance and de Sitter swampland criteria, while giving acceptable tensor-to-scalar ratio r and scalar spectral index ns for two example potentials?

sources.title: Kinetic axion dark matter in string corrected <math display="inline" id="d1e782" altimg="si6.svg"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>R</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> gravity

evidence.text: How does an axion-dependent Gauss–Bonnet coupling, constrained to give luminal tensor propagation, change kinetic-misalignment axion dynamics, inflationary observables and the proposed postinflationary stiff era in R² gravity?

sources.title: Inflationary Dynamics and Swampland Criteria for Modified Gauss-Bonnet Gravity Compatible with GW170817

evidence.text: Can rescaled Einstein–Gauss–Bonnet inflation with imposed luminal tensor propagation yield viable scalar observables and blue tensor tilt, satisfy Swampland tests or tracking, and modify reheating and primordial gravitational-wave spectra?

sources.title: Swampland program for hypergeometric inflation scenarios in rescaled gravity

evidence.text: Can hypergeometric scalar–Gauss–Bonnet couplings in rescaled Einstein–Hilbert gravity generate inflationary potentials compatible with the Planck observations cited by the authors and with the adopted swampland conjectures?

sources.title: Hypergeometric potential inflation and swampland program in rescaled gravity with stringy corrections

evidence.text: Can differential constraints on a scalar–Gauss–Bonnet coupling generate hypergeometric inflationary potentials that satisfy the paper's observational benchmarks and swampland criteria while maintaining small slow-roll parameters in rescaled gravity?

sources.title: Primordial black holes in SB SUSY Gauss-Bonnet inflation

evidence.text: Can scalar–Gauss–Bonnet coupling reconcile the low-scale spontaneously broken SUSY inflationary potential with CMB constraints while producing primordial black holes, induced gravitational waves, and satisfying proposed swampland criteria?

sources.title: New Effects in Multifield Cosmology Coupled to the Gauss-Bonnet Term

evidence.text: How does scalar coupling to the Gauss–Bonnet term modify two-field rapid-turn inflation, its potential slow-roll relations and consistency conditions, and the possibility of phantom-like dark energy?

sources.title: Higher Curvature Corrections to Primordial Fluctuations in Slow-roll Inflation

evidence.text: Derive background equations and slow-roll consistency conditions, introducing three curvature-coupling parameters in addition to the conventional potential slow-roll parameters.

sources.title: Inflation driven by Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity

evidence.text: Vary the action and reduce it to homogeneous background equations. The Bianchi identity makes only two background equations independent. For V=0, specify H(t), reconstruct ξ(t) with an integrating factor, and determine Φ(t); the nonconstant example requires numerical integration.

sources.title: Viable Inflation in Scalar-Gauss-Bonnet Gravity and Reconstruction from Observational Indices

evidence.text: Bottom-up reconstruction first specifies H(N) and r(N), solves for ξ(N), then obtains φ(N) and V(N) from approximate background equations. The resulting ns(N) is tested separately; ξ(φ) and V(φ) require invertibility of φ(N).

sources.title: Swampland implications of GW170817-compatible Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity

evidence.text: Use a monotonic scalar as the evolution coordinate, expand time derivatives, impose an explicit term hierarchy, and solve the remaining algebraic trajectory equation. Here the constraint is tensor luminality and the output parametrizes single-field inflation.

sources.title: Pleasant behavior of swampland conjectures in the face of specific inflationary models

evidence.text: Uses slow-roll potential expressions ε1=(1−λ)(V′/V)²/2 and ε2=−2(1−λ)[V″/V−(V′/V)²], together with ns=1−2ε1−ε2 and r=16(1−λ)ε1. These are formulas adopted by the paper, without independent verification in this pass.

sources.title: Kinetic axion dark matter in string corrected <math display="inline" id="d1e782" altimg="si6.svg"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>R</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> gravity

evidence.text: Construct an autonomous system using e-fold time, dimensionless kinetic, potential, curvature, Gauss–Bonnet and fluid variables. Classify fixed points through eigenvalues, and impose an additional compatibility equation inherited from the tensor-speed constraint.

sources.title: Swampland implications of GW170817-compatible Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity

evidence.text: The adopted criteria create a tension between a steep potential and small tensor production in minimally coupled canonical inflation. The paper asks whether the Gauss–Bonnet interaction changes this relationship.

sources.title: Revisiting Scalar Tensor inflation by swampland criteria and Reheating

evidence.text: Can a scalar-dependent gravitational coupling accommodate slow-roll inflation, the observed scalar/tensor spectra, and the paper's swampland cuts? The study also asks which effective reheating equations of state give positive, relatively short expansion histories.

sources.title: On the existence of singularity free solutions in quadratic gravity

evidence.text: Which conditions on a scalar-dependent Gauss–Bonnet coupling ensure the existence of classical singularity-free solutions in spatially flat FRW cosmology?

sources.title: Gauss-Bonnet Inflation

evidence.text: Can a scalar coupled to the Gauss–Bonnet invariant generate early de Sitter expansion and an exit without an imposed scalar self-potential, after neglecting the Einstein–Hilbert term in a proposed strong-gravity regime?

sources.title: Singularity free cosmological solutions in quadratic gravity

evidence.text: Can a scalar field coupled to the quadratic Gauss–Bonnet invariant support nonsingular open and closed FRW cosmologies, and can the singular families be confined to only part of the classical phase space?

sources.title: CMB from a Gauss-Bonnet-induced de Sitter fixed point

evidence.text: Can de Sitter fixed points sustained by a balance between a massive scalar potential and a scalar-dependent Gauss-Bonnet coupling generate CMB-compatible fluctuations, and thereby constrain the coupling function?

sources.title: Rectifying Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet Inflation in View of GW170817

evidence.text: Can Einstein–Gauss–Bonnet inflation be organized into analytically manageable scalar-field equations while imposing luminal tensor propagation, and can particular coupling–potential pairs reproduce the paper's Planck-2018 benchmarks for the scalar tilt and tensor-to-scalar ratio?

sources.title: EFT approach to black hole scalarization and its compatibility with cosmic evolution

evidence.text: Can a scalar–gravity EFT containing curvature operators through cubic order support black-hole scalarization while remaining compatible with inflation, standard cosmological evolution and a late-time approach to General Relativity?

sources.title: Renormalizable Cosmology Based on Gauss-Bonnet Theory with Torsion

evidence.text: Can a gauge-matter construction with independent torsion and Gauss-Bonnet corrections provide a renormalizable cosmological framework, modified stress-energy and inflationary equations, and a route to observational effects on cosmic expansion?

sources.title: Primordial black holes in non-minimal Gauss–Bonnet inflation in light of the PTA data

evidence.text: Can a two-part inflaton–Gauss–Bonnet coupling make monomial inflation compatible with CMB constraints while enhancing small-scale curvature perturbations enough for PBHs and scalar-induced gravitational waves, including a possible PTA signal?

sources.title: Swampland criteria for rescaled Einstein-Hilbert gravity with string corrections

evidence.text: Can canonical slow-roll inflation with a rescaled Einstein-Hilbert term and, separately, Gauss-Bonnet or Chern-Simons corrections satisfy the paper's Swampland tests and historical Planck constraints, possibly with a blue tensor tilt?

sources.title: Gauss–Bonnet Inflation and the String Swampland

evidence.text: Can a scalar-dependent curvature coupling change inflationary observables enough to accommodate a steep potential and a small field excursion?

sources.title: Swampland implications of GW170817-compatible Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity

evidence.text: The setting describes inflation driven by one canonical scalar coupled to the Gauss–Bonnet invariant. This interaction changes homogeneous evolution and cosmological perturbation propagation and normalization.
